passages.title: The Instructions We Tested
paragraphs: Our class wrote instructions for folding a paper hat. I thought mine were clear until my partner tried them without watching me. She folded the wrong corner, and her hat became a narrow pocket. I wanted to show her, but the teacher asked me to improve the words instead. I added a small diagram（示意图） and explained which edge should face upwards. My partner tried again and succeeded. To find out whether instructions work, it helps to watch someone use them. What seems obvious（显而易见的） to the writer may puzzle the reader.

passages.title: The Lunchbox That Was Too Full
paragraphs: I packed my lunchbox with everything I thought I might want: rice, vegetables, fruit and two large sandwiches. At lunchtime, I could not finish half of it. The next morning, Dad suggested thinking about how much I usually ate. We chose smaller portions（份量） and put them in separate spaces. I still had different foods, but less was left over. By Friday, I knew which amounts suited me. Planning a meal meant more than filling a box. I needed to take into account my own appetite（胃口） as well.

passages.title: My Grandfather’s Handwriting
paragraphs: Grandfather sent me a letter written with a fountain pen（钢笔）. Some letters joined（连接） together in ways I had never seen. I could read most of it, but one sentence puzzled me. Instead of guessing, I called him and asked. He read it aloud, then told me about writing letters before he owned a phone. I tried answering him by hand. My first page had several crossed-out words, yet I kept going. The reply took longer than a message, but I enjoyed choosing each sentence with care and signing my name.

passages.title: The Notice at Eye Level
paragraphs: We put a sign beside our classroom door to remind pupils to return sports equipment. After a week, very little changed. Then a younger pupil asked what the sign said. It was above her head, hidden by a hanging coat. We moved it lower and cleared the space around it. Soon, more balls appeared in the basket. We had spent time choosing the words but forgotten where people would read them. A helpful reminder（提醒） needs to be easy to see. Its position（位置） can make a difference to whether it works.

passages.title: The Skipping Rope Rhythm
paragraphs: I could skip alone, but joining a long rope turned by two classmates felt difficult. I kept jumping before the rope reached me. Our teacher suggested watching its rhythm first. I stood beside the group and counted quietly as the rope touched the ground. Then I stepped in at the right moment and jumped three times. Everyone cheered. I still missed several turns afterwards, but I knew what to practise. Keeping up with others began with listening and watching. Speed mattered less than finding the same rhythm（节奏） and timing（时机）.

passages.title: A Drawing Made of Dots
paragraphs: In art class, we made pictures using only tiny dots. I chose an orange fish in blue water. Close up, the colours looked separate, and the fish seemed rough. When I walked to the other side of the room, the dots joined into a smoother picture. I returned to my desk and added a few darker dots beneath the fish. Those small marks suggested a shadow. The picture changed depending on my distance（距离） from it. Sometimes I need to step back before I can see how the details（细节） work together.

passages.title: The Library Shelf Number
paragraphs: I wanted a book about volcanoes, but the library had many shelves. I asked the librarian to help me search the catalogue（目录）. Beside the title was a number that matched a section of the shelves. We followed the signs, checked the labels and found the book between two others about Earth. The number was more than a mark on its spine（书脊）. It was part of a system（系统） that helped readers find things. Once I understood how to look up a book, the large room felt much less confusing（令人困惑的）.

passages.title: The Day We Followed a Visitor
paragraphs: Our school invited a parent to try finding the music room using only our signs. We followed quietly and noted where she stopped. At one corner, an arrow pointed towards two different corridors（走廊）. She chose the wrong one. Afterwards, we changed the sign and added another beside the stairs. A second visitor reached the room without help. We knew the school too well to notice the problem ourselves. Seeing it through a visitor’s eyes helped us deal with a small difficulty（困难） that had been easy to overlook（忽略）.

passages.title: The Two-Minute Tidy
paragraphs: My desk became crowded again soon after I cleaned it. I usually waited until nothing could fit beside my notebook. Then I tried a small change. Before leaving school, I spent two minutes returning pencils, closing books and throwing away tiny scraps. On busy afternoons, I only cleared one corner. After a week, I could find my ruler without searching under everything. A little regular effort（努力） was easier than one huge tidy. I did not have a perfect desk, but I could keep it in order with less trouble（麻烦）.

passages.title: A Word with Two Meanings
paragraphs: In a story, a boy sat on a river bank. I pictured a building where people kept money and wondered why he was sitting on it. My teacher asked me to read the next sentence. The boy was fishing beneath a tree. Suddenly, the meaning became clear. The same word can describe different things, and nearby words help us choose the right meaning. I drew two pictures beside “bank” in my notebook. Now I pay attention to the whole sentence when a familiar word appears in an unusual（不寻常的） context（语境）.

passages.title: The Boat Made from Clay
paragraphs: A small ball of clay sank when I dropped it into a bowl of water. Our teacher asked whether I could make the same clay float. I pressed it into a wide, hollow（空心的） boat and placed it gently on the surface. This time, it stayed up. Its new shape pushed aside more water before water could enter it. We added small counters（计数片） until the boat sat too low and filled. I had not changed the amount of clay. Changing its shape was enough to make a difference to the result.

passages.title: The Colours on the Wet Path
paragraphs: After a shower, the path outside looked darker than before. I noticed the same change when I wet part of a pale stone. The damp patch became deeper in colour, though the stone itself had not been painted. Our teacher explained that water changes how light travels through and reflects（反射） from the surface. As the stone dried, its usual appearance returned. I drew two versions in my notebook. Rain had given me a new reason to take a closer look at an ordinary surface（表面） and its changing appearance（外观）.

passages.title: The Air inside the Ball
paragraphs: Our playground ball felt soft and hardly bounced. A teacher used a pump to add more air. Soon, the ball held its round shape and bounced higher. Air takes up space and can push against the inside of a ball. We compared the ball before and after pumping by dropping it from the same height. I had thought an empty-looking space contained nothing. Now I could feel what was inside, even though I could not see it. A simple game helped me learn about air and its pressure（压力） through an experiment（实验）.

passages.title: A Handle Far from the Hinge
paragraphs: The classroom door was heavy. When I pushed near its hinge（铰链）, it was difficult to move. Pushing near the handle was much easier. Our teacher explained that the distance from the hinge matters when we turn a door. We tried gently, keeping our fingers away from the edges. The door had not become lighter; we were pushing in a more useful place. Afterwards, I noticed where handles sat on other doors. Their position（位置） made sense. Everyday objects often help us make use of simple principles（原理） without thinking about them.

passages.title: The Leaf Rubbing Collection
paragraphs: We collected fallen leaves of different shapes and placed them under thin paper. I rubbed a crayon gently across the top. Lines appeared where the leaf’s veins（叶脉） pressed against the paper. One leaf had a single strong middle line, while another spread its lines like fingers. We labelled each rubbing and compared the patterns. I used to notice only the colour of leaves. Now I saw the smaller structures as well. Side by side, our pages showed how much variety（多样性） could be found in one small collection（收集品）.

passages.title: The Earthworm’s Underground Work
paragraphs: After gardening with Dad, I noticed an earthworm moving into the soil. We left it where it was and looked at the tiny opening. Dad explained that earthworms make tunnels（通道） as they move underground. These spaces can help air and water enter the soil. Earthworms also help break down dead plant material（物质）. Their work is difficult to see from above, but it changes the ground around them. I used to think the soil was still and quiet. Beneath my feet, a whole world was busy with activity.

passages.title: The Clock Repairer’s Window
paragraphs: A shop window near our home was full of clocks. Some had long swinging pendulums（钟摆）; others were small enough for a bedside table. One afternoon, the repairer showed me a tray of tiny parts. He explained that different clocks work in different ways, so he must examine each one carefully. I listened to the soft ticking around us. When a repaired clock began striking, he smiled. It had taken days to find the fault. Working out what had gone wrong needed patience（耐心）, good tools and close observation（观察）.

passages.title: The Street Name on the Corner
paragraphs: I knew our street by its shops, but my aunt asked for its name when she came to visit. I had to look at the sign on the corner. Later, I noticed signs at other junctions（交叉路口） and wrote down the names on my route to school. A shop might close or change, while a street name usually lasted longer. I could now explain our address more clearly. The signs had always been there. I simply had not realised how useful those labels（标识） were for finding my way around the neighbourhood（街区）.

passages.title: The Market Stall Scales
paragraphs: At a fruit stall, I chose some pears and placed them in a bowl. Before weighing them, the seller checked that the empty bowl did not add to the displayed weight. Then she placed the pears inside. I watched the numbers settle. The total weight of bowl and fruit was different from the weight of the fruit alone. At home, I tried the same idea with kitchen scales. Accurate measurement（测量） needed more than reading a number. I also had to think about what the number actually represented（代表）.

passages.title: The Morning Refill Round
paragraphs: At our local café, a worker checked the water station before opening. She filled clean jugs, arranged glasses and wiped the table. During our visit, I saw her return several times to refill（重新装满） the jugs. The task looked small, but dozens of customers used the station. If she forgot, many people would need to ask for help. I thanked her while returning my glass. Some useful work happens so quietly that we hardly notice it. Making sure things are ready can be an important part of good service（服务）.

passages.title: The Fox and the Small Umbrella
paragraphs: A fox bought an umbrella just wide enough to cover his head. He liked how light it was. When rain came, his long tail became wet. He blamed the umbrella maker, who asked whether he had checked its size before buying it. The fox had only looked at the bright pattern. Next time, he opened several umbrellas and tried them carefully. He chose a plain one that covered his tail too. As well as looking attractive, a useful object must suit（适合） the person who needs it and its purpose（用途）.

passages.title: The Bear’s List of Guests
paragraphs: A bear invited his forest friends to dinner and planned a meal of fish. Before cooking, he read his guest list again. Rabbit, deer and squirrel were coming too. He realised that one dish would not suit everyone. He asked his guests what they liked and prepared several choices. At dinner, bowls of leaves, nuts and other food stood beside the fish. Nobody had to eat exactly what the bear enjoyed. A warm welcome（欢迎） included thinking about others in advance. The bear’s careful planning made everyone feel included（被接纳的）.

passages.title: One Book and Two Bookmarks
paragraphs: My sister and I wanted to read the same adventure book. We agreed to share it, but she read much faster than I did. When she mentioned a secret door, I covered my ears. I had not reached that part yet! We made a rule: no talking about later events unless both of us had read them. Two bookmarks kept our places, and we took turns with the book after dinner. Sharing a story also meant respecting another reader’s pace（速度）. We could enjoy ourselves without spoiling the next surprise（意外之事）.

passages.title: The Answer I Changed
paragraphs: In a group discussion, I said that our class trip should include three museums in one day. My partner disagreed and showed us the travel times. There would be little time to explore any of them. At first, I defended my plan because it was mine. Then I imagined rushing through each building. I suggested visiting just one museum and spending longer there. Changing my mind did not mean I had lost the discussion. It meant I was willing to use new information（信息） to reach a better decision（决定）.

passages.title: The Compliment I Remembered
paragraphs: After my talk, several classmates said, “Good job.” I was pleased, but one comment stayed with me. A friend said the example about her little brother had helped her understand my main idea. She told me exactly which part had worked. The next time I prepared a talk, I remembered her words and chose another clear example. I also tried giving more specific（具体的） praise to others. Pointing out something useful helped them know what to keep doing. A thoughtful compliment（赞美） could become advice for the next attempt.

passages.title: The Table We Moved Together
paragraphs: We needed to move a light classroom table to make space for a game. Four of us lifted at different moments, and one corner nearly caught a chair. Our teacher asked us to stop and put it down. We cleared the route, chose someone to count and lifted together on “three”. The table moved smoothly. It had not changed, and neither had our strength. What changed was our coordination（配合）. Working together meant agreeing on when and how to act, not simply adding more hands to the same task（任务）.

passages.title: A Plan for a Rainy Sports Day
paragraphs: We had practised outdoor games all week, but rain arrived on sports day. For a while, everyone complained. Then our teacher asked which activities could work in the hall. Running races would not fit, but we could try balance games and gentle ball activities. We moved the equipment and changed the timetable. The day felt different from our plan, yet we still laughed and cheered. Having a goal did not mean following only one route. A flexible（灵活的） plan gave us room to carry on when the conditions（条件） changed.

passages.title: The Sandwich in the Story
paragraphs: I wrote a story about a child who lost a sandwich. Every sentence began with “Then”. When I read it aloud, the events sounded like a list. My teacher asked what the child could hear, smell and feel. I added the rustle（沙沙声） of the empty bag and the child’s growing surprise. I did not need a much longer story. A few well-chosen details helped the scene become clearer. Reading my work aloud also helped me cut out words that added nothing. My second draft（草稿） had more life.

passages.title: The Skill I Could Share
paragraphs: My younger cousin wanted to learn how to tie a bow. I showed him quickly, but his fingers could not follow mine. I slowed down and sat beside him so we could look in the same direction. We used two thick ribbons of different colours. After several tries, he made a loose bow and grinned. Teaching something familiar made me notice its smaller steps. I had to break it down into actions he could practise. His small achievement（成就） made me appreciate both his effort（努力） and the skill itself.

passages.title: The Good Thing I Almost Missed
paragraphs: On Friday, I told Mum that my week had been terrible. I had lost a game and forgotten a homework book. She listened, then asked whether anything else had happened. I remembered helping a classmate, enjoying a funny story and finally learning a difficult song. I had left those happy moments out of my story. The problems were real, but they were not the whole week. I did not need to pretend everything was perfect. I only needed to look back on it with a more balanced（全面客观的） view（看法）.
